result:
The proposed formula checks out in every case I tested, though I did not prove it in general.

- **r = 1:** K₂-free means S is empty, so the value is 0. The formula gives p−1−2·((p−1)/2) = 0.
- **r = 2:** Triangle-free means S is sum-free. The largest sum-free sets in ℤ_p have size ⌊(p+1)/3⌋, and the middle-third interval is symmetric. For p = 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 the formula gives 2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 6, which matches ⌊(p+1)/3⌋ in each case.
- **r = p−1:** The full set S = ℤ_p∖{0} gives K_p, so |S| ≤ p−3. Taking S = ℤ_p∖{0, ±a} gives a K_p-free graph, so the value is p−3. The formula gives p−3.
- **Large r (r+1 > (p−1)/2):** For S = ℤ_p∖{0, ±a}, the complement of Cay(ℤ_p, S) is a p-cycle, so the clique number is (p−1)/2. That is below r+1, so p−3 is achieved. The formula gives ⌊(p−1)/(r+1)⌋ = 1 and hence p−3.
- **General construction:** Take S = {x : m ≤ |x| ≤ (p−1)/2} with m = ⌊(p−1)/(r+1)⌋+1. A clique needs elements pairwise at cyclic distance at least m, so the clique number is ⌊p/m⌋ ≤ r. This gives |S| = p−1−2⌊(p−1)/(r+1)⌋, which matches the formula. For p = 13, r = 3 it gives 6.

I did not independently verify that no better construction exists for all (p, r). The formula agrees with the known extremal value in the cases checked, so I accept it.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
